chunks: Ali (peace be upon him) from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

If a woman is divorced, then her husband dies while she is in her waiting period (iddah) from him, she does not become permanently forbidden to him; for she inherits him and he inherits her as long as she is in the blood of her second menstruation from the first two divorces. If he divorces her a third time, then she does not inherit her husband anything, nor does he inherit her.
ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance rules for a divorced woman whose husband dies during her waiting period?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir clarifies the specific condition under which a revocably divorced wife inherits her husband upon his death: she must remain in the 'blood phase' (damm) of her second menstruation following the initial two divorces. This detail highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the precise timing of the iddah period, distinguishing it from the general rule that a wife in iddah inherits, and underscores the finality of the third divorce which severs all inheritance ties.
